panels.description: Dusk inside the modest Keel apartment: handmade quilts, repaired furniture, shelves of old books, faded family photographs, potted plants in recycled containers and two ration-marked water jugs by the door. Grandmother sits in a worn chair folding and refolding a cloth. A tall bookshelf has one worn blue book isolated on its top shelf. Alex stands in the doorway with his backpack. Reserve the upper-left for dialogue.

Alex kneels beside Grandmother at eye level. Her hands continue folding the cloth; his smile is gentle and tired. Keep the bookshelf and blue book visible. Reserve separate upper-left and upper-right zones for the exchange.
Grandmother’s fog clears. Her face becomes startlingly steady and deliberate while Alex remains softly out of focus behind her. Reserve the upper-left for her line.

Grandmother points toward the isolated blue book. Its spine bears a faint balanced water-drop mark. Alex reaches up on his toes, puzzled, while warm room light falls behind him. Keep the book and pointing hand clear. Use a left vertical lettering column for Grandmother’s instructions and a right column for Alex’s response.

items.speaker: GRANDMOTHER
items.text: Of course. Alex. I knew that.

items.speaker: GRANDMOTHER
items.text: Eighteen. Oh. Then there's something your father wanted you to have.

items.speaker: GRANDMOTHER
items.text: Get me the blue book, would you? Top shelf.

items.speaker: GRANDMOTHER
items.text: Your father never let anyone else touch it.
